key_insight: A proposed universal scaling law links droplet projection area to key impact loads, capturing the effects of initial droplet shape and orientation.
engineering_relevance: The framework could improve wind turbine leading-edge erosion predictions beyond idealized spherical-droplet, normal-incidence assumptions.
method: Couple incompressible multiphase flow simulations with finite element analysis through fluid–structure interaction.
Investigate impact dynamics for droplets with arbitrary shapes and orientations.
Relate impact-loading metrics to projection area determined from initial droplet geometry.
evidence_signal: Simulations show positively correlated peak pressure, affected area at peak pressure, and peak force, with peak-force timing scaling inversely; the abstract provides no quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish experimental validation or the scaling law’s applicability across real blade materials and operating conditions.
paper_title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
